Motion Picture House is a large-scale audiovisual installation and art gallery, purpose built to showcase KID A MNESIA. It features a 75-minute movie that blends the architecture of the house with the world of the film which was built from art created by Thom Yorke and Stanley Donwood during the Kid A and Amnesiac recording sessions. The movie and surrounding galleries also premiere a new mix of the songs from KID A MNESIA in spatial audio.

This song is about a car crash Thom Yorke was in with his girlfriend in 1987. She suffered whiplash, but he was fine. Says Yorke: "Has an airbag saved my life? Nah... but I tell you something, every time you have a near accident, instead of just sighing and carrying on, you should pull over, get out of the car and run down the street screaming 'I'm BACK! I'm ALIVE! My life has started again today!' In fact, you should do that every time you get out of a car. We're just riding on those things - we're not really in control of them."
--
This was built around a looped 3-second sample of drummer Philip Selway, who cited instrumental hip hop producer DJ Shadow as an inspiration.

The title is a reference to Marvin the Paranoid Android in the book "The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy" by Douglas Adams.

The song's structure is patterned after "Happiness Is A Warm Gun" by The Beatles. Both are clearly a collection of other, shorter pieces of songs put together into one.

The guitar solo at the end of the song was written by guitarist Jonny Greenwood. It was not originally intended for the song, but something was needed to close the song and this solo was in the right key and right tempo. Thom Yorke has said the unlikely inspiration for "Electioneering" was Noam Chomsky — he'd been reading the media critic's work and channeled the venal-politician voice into the lyric, partly as a critique of Radiohead's own grueling promotional schedule for the album. Ed O'Brien put it bluntly: the album campaign was starting to feel like a political campaign. Yorke was also turning over the 1990 UK Poll Tax Riots in his head while writing — the scenes of people breaking down the gates of Downing Street. He's called the song "an incitement to riot."
